source_title: Sahel Crisis 2012: Ensuring Food Security and Protecting Livelihoods, Information Note No. 1
issuer: FAO Sub-regional Emergency and Rehabilitation Office, West Africa/Sahel
place: Sahel region (CILSS aggregate); Chad, Mauritania, Senegal
reading: Sahel cereal 16.6 million tonnes in 2011/12, 25 percent below the 2010/11 record and 2 percent below the previous five years. Chad, Mauritania and Senegal fell 50, 52 and 31 percent from 2010/11. A footnote revises Chad to -39 percent nationally. The aggregate is the CILSS Sahel, not the ten workbook countries, and it is a forecast.

source_title: Sub-Saharan Africa Outlook and Situation Report, RS-85-10
location_in_source: PDF page 15 (scanned, read by text extraction)
causes_named_by_source: below-normal rainfall; pests; government investment and pricing policies; civil wars
reading: Food grain production was 20 to 30 percent below normal in 1984, and over 5 million tons were produced. The report names rainfall, army worms, government policy and civil war together.

source_title: Food, Population, and Famine: Bengal 1943-44 and Bangladesh 1974-75
issuer: Tim Dyson, IUSSP International Population Conference paper
reading: The aman crop harvested at the end of 1974 was 700,000 tons below 1973's, and the author ties it to the flooding. The sentence does not name its data source. Table 2 in the paper is food-grain availability, not production.

source_title: Conflict, drought impact crop prospects in Syria, UN agency says
change: about 52 percent below; wheat area about 15 percent below
baseline: 2001-2011 average; area against the average of recent years
causes_named_by_source: drought (rainfall deficits); conflict; input availability and prices
reading: FAO expected 2014 wheat at 1.97 million tonnes, some 52 percent below the 2001-2011 average. Drought and conflict are named together.

source_title: Erratic weather and prolonged conflict take toll on Syria's agricultural output
reading: Wheat fell to 1.2 million tons in 2018, about two-thirds of 2017 levels. FAO names weather in the seventh year of conflict.

source_title: GIEWS Country Brief: Yemen
causes_named_by_source: ongoing conflict; flash floods and landslides in July 2016
reading: Total 2016 cereal production about 480,000 tonnes, 11 percent below 2015 and 37 percent below the five-year average. Conflict and July 2016 floods are named together.

source_title: GIEWS Country Brief Yemen 10 February 2017
reading: HTTP 403. The same brief was read from the FAO archive PDF instead.

source_title: Haiti's damaged food sector slowly begins to mend
issuer: FAO Newsroom, reporting the FAO/WFP Crop and Food Security Assessment Mission
causes_named_by_source: January 2010 earthquake; late start of the spring rains
reading: FAO/WFP forecast 2010 cereals at 503,600 tonnes, 9 percent below 2009. Spring maize fell 8 percent and sorghum 4 percent from 2009. Irrigated rice was expected up 15 percent. Earthquake damage and a late rainy season are named together. The mission report itself was not opened.

source_title: GIEWS Country Brief: Lao People's Democratic Republic
causes_named_by_source: poor rains associated with the El Niño episode
reading: FAO puts 2015 rice at 3.2 million tonnes, 4 percent below the 2014 record, and maize at 1.1 million tonnes, 5 percent below 2014, after poor El Niño rains. The 20 December 2016 brief gives 2016 paddy at 4 million tonnes, a 5 percent recovery; rice and paddy are not the same unit.

source_title: GIEWS Country Brief: Timor-Leste
change: 6 and 30 percent below (rice); 8 and 21 percent below (maize)
reading: FAO forecast 2016 rice at 60,000 tonnes, 6 percent below 2015 and 30 percent below the five-year average, and maize at 60,000 tonnes, 8 and 21 percent below. 2015 was already reduced. El Niño dry weather is named.

source_title: Rebuilding Livelihoods in Communities Affected by El Niño in Timor-Leste, TCP/TIM/3609
reading: HTTP 403. A search snippet quoting maize -13 and rice -71 percent was not verified and is not used.

source_title: Special Report: Crop and Food Supply Situation in Sierra Leone
change: about 45 percent of pre-war; 24.4 percent below 1998
causes_named_by_source: civil war; displacement of farm families
reading: Paddy 248,220 tonnes in 1999, about 45 percent of pre-war (1990) and 24.4 percent below 1998. Table 1 (MAFE) gives 543.7 thousand tonnes in 1990 and 411.1 in 1991. The report calls its estimates provisional and based on incomplete data.

source_title: Special Report: FAO/GIEWS Crop Assessment Mission to Liberia
reading: 1995 rice was at most 23 percent of the pre-civil-war level (Table 1: 56,196 to 64,426 tonnes). The mission calls its estimates highly tentative, with no systematic survey since 1989.

source_title: FAO/WFP Crop and Food Supply Assessment Mission to Liberia
causes_named_by_source: war and displacement; small plots; rebel incursions in Lofa
reading: 2000 paddy 144,000 tonnes against 259,000 in 1988; milled 94,000 tonnes is 55 percent of pre-war. No official crop data has been collected since 1989, and the mission assumed 500 kg per household.

source_title: More poison than words can describe: what did people die of after the 1783 Laki eruption in Iceland?
reading: No crop quantity. The paper says haze damaged Icelandic grass, and that records show no evidence of harvest failure in west and central Europe in 1783. The workbook footprint is 26 countries.
Searches found qualitative 2015-2016 drought reports (RNZ, OCHA, World Vision) and no quantified crop figure. GIEWS has no Solomon Islands brief. Nothing opened.

source_title: FAO/WFP Crop and Food Supply Assessment Mission to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (Special Report)
reading: Total 1996 grain about 4.3 million tons including milled rice; flood losses cut output by a further 300,000 tons, leaving 2.84 million tons net of milled rice and maize. Based on government discussions and mission estimates; no land classification maps.

source_title: FAO/WFP Crop and Food Supply Assessment Mission to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (Special Report)
causes_named_by_source: worst drought for decades; Typhoon Winnie tidal waves
reading: 1997 maize 1.138 million tons, some 51 percent below 1996 and the lowest on record; paddy 2.35 million tons (1.52 milled). Maize and rice 2.66 million tons milled equivalent. Area figures are official, yields are mission estimates. The text after character 39,950 was not read verbatim.

source_title: 7121.0 Agricultural Commodities, Australia, 2002-03 (media release: Drought hits agriculture hard in 2002-03)
place: Australia; New South Wales; Western Australia
change: wheat down 58 percent; NSW down 69 percent to 2.5 Mt; WA down 48 percent to 4.0 Mt; barley down 53 percent
reading: Wheat fell 58 percent to 10.1 million tonnes in 2002-03; NSW fell 69 percent to 2.5 and WA 48 percent to 4.0. Barley fell 53 percent to 3.9 despite 4 percent more plantings. One season of the 2000-2009 registry window; van Dijk 2013 says production over the whole drought rose on more area.

source_title: Southern Africa Situation Report, September 2016
causes_named_by_source: El Niño; driest season in 35 years
reading: Regional shortfall of nearly 9.3 million tonnes of cereal production in 2015/16. Southern Africa is not on the ENSO2015_2016 workbook sheet, which lists Australia, South and Southeast Asia, and the Americas.

source_title: GIEWS Country Brief: Ukraine
causes_named_by_source: active fighting and the economic impact of the war: field access, labour, costs, low farmgate prices
reading: FAO forecast 2022 cereals at 51 million tonnes, almost 30 percent below the five-year average and 40 percent below the exceptional 2021 output. The brief names the war's effect on access, labour, costs and prices.
